This is an **ungraded practice** page. Choose one option and work on it after the lab. It uses the code you wrote in Session 14 and the models of Session 13.

## Option A: Couzin model

Theory: [The Couzin Model](couzin-model.qmd).

- Implement the Couzin rules and motion in two dimensions.
- Animate the individuals moving. Reuse the structure of [Animation](vicsek-animation.qmd).
- Implement the group polarization $p_{\text{group}}$ and the angular momentum $m_{\text{group}}$ defined in @couzin2002collective. Compare $p_{\text{group}}$ with the [Vicsek order parameter](vicsek-order-parameter.qmd).
- Explore the widths $\Delta r_o$ and $\Delta r_a$ and find the four collective behaviours described by @couzin2002collective: swarm, torus, dynamic parallel group and highly parallel group.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Optional extension

- Add sliders to change parameters in real time.
- Test collective memory: slowly increase $\Delta r_o$ and then decrease it again, and check whether the group state follows the same path both ways.
- Implement the model in 3D, as in the original paper.
:::

## Option B: Vicsek model with predator avoidance

Guide: [Predator Avoidance](vicsek-predator.qmd).

The predator can be a fixed point, a random walker, or your mouse cursor. Particles inside the predator radius turn directly away from it, as in the Couzin repulsion rule.

- Implement the full Vicsek animation from [Animation](vicsek-animation.qmd).
- Add the predator avoidance rule and draw the predator.
- Explore the parameter space. How does the predator affect the order parameter? Is there a regime where the group splits and later merges again? Can you find a regime where the particles escape the predator?

## Exit question

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise

In the Vicsek model you double both $N$ and $L^2$, keeping the density and the noise fixed. Which features of the order parameter curve $\varphi(\eta)$ should stay the same, and which should change?
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

The density $\rho = N/L^2$ is unchanged, so in the ordered phase $\varphi$ should be about the same. At high noise, $\varphi$ is set by the finite-size floor of order $1/\sqrt{N}$, which decreases by a factor $\sqrt{2}$. The transition region should become sharper. This is the pattern in Figure 2(a) of @vicsek1995novel.
:::
